claims.text: A machine-learning workflow combining partial high-temperature calorimetric and dilatometric data with CALPHAD and computational thermodynamic databases can accurately predict melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across a broad range of HEAs.
HEAs are composed of five or more principal elements in equiatomic or near-equiatomic ratios.
HEAs exhibit complex atomic interactions and local lattice distortions.

Physicochemical descriptors such as atomic-radius mismatch, elemental melting points, and mixing enthalpies can be integrated with sparse experiments and thermodynamic calculations to predict fusion behavior.
Direct high-temperature experimental characterization across HEA composition space is resource-intensive.
High-temperature DSC and drop calorimetry are costly and time-consuming.
The model can establish useful statistical correlations between physicochemical descriptors, partial experimental inputs, and computed thermodynamic behavior.
Adding targeted calorimetry and dilatometry results iteratively will refine the model's predictive correlations.
CALPHAD calculations use thermodynamic databases that supply phase Gibbs energies as functions of pressure, temperature, and composition.
CALPHAD is an efficient and practically accurate tool for multicomponent phase-diagram calculation and HEA design.
Combining experimental trends with computational predictions enables interpolation and potential extrapolation of melting behavior and fusion properties across HEA compositions.
The workflow will predict melting temperatures with less than 5% error relative to direct measurements.
The workflow will predict enthalpy and entropy of fusion with similarly bounded errors of approximately less than 5%.
The workflow will predict volume changes at melting with similarly bounded errors of approximately less than 5%.
The resulting estimates will be reliable enough to guide experimental alloy development.
Standalone CALPHAD predictions are limited by incomplete thermodynamic data.
The workflow is primarily applicable to HEA compositions lying within the established ranges of its training data.
Performance may deteriorate for very non-equiatomic, phase-segregated, poorly characterized, or sparsely sampled compositions.

contradictions.description: The expected error bound is stated as below 5%, whereas falsification requires consistent errors above 10% and calls that threshold an established uncertainty bound. This leaves an unresolved 5–10% range in which the stated performance target fails but the approach is not ruled out.
